Opus-1 read SKILL.md, references/library-design.md and references/ex_unit.md with Read (the last before writing a throwaway test in .verify, which it deleted), and the other four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all five. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a row with a +02:00 offset), the top five with ties broken by customer id, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an amount with trailing text, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 raise FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it straight to Decimal.parse/1, which no listed rule covers.

Rules changed since 0814e8d, graded against the current text. In SKILL.md only One expression per line, and tabular clauses, and the `do:` rule changed on this case's list; the changes to references/macros.md and references/processes.md do not touch Decide whether you need a process. One expression per line is decided by "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line, and a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes in `do ... end`", and the `do:` rule lost its 0814e8d sentence "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." and the matching example. Sonnet-2 line 243 (for %Order{status: :completed} = order <- orders, do: order) is clean under both rules by the new sentence; under the 0814e8d text it would have been a `do:` violation, as the 2026-10-31-check-2 macro-dsl grade counted such lines. Haiku-2 lines 146-148 keep a one-expression `for` in `do ... end`. The new sentence names no length, so this is a judgement: the one-line form would be 93 characters after the indentation, past the about 70 characters the `->` rule sets for the `fn` shape the `for` sentence says it reads like, so the block is held clean; if the sentence is meant without that limit, haiku-2 is violated on this rule at lines 146-148. No run puts a `for` body of several expressions or a nested construct on one line.

Verdicts worth checking. Enum/Map, sonnet-2 line 243 is a new shape with no earlier grade: no previous order-report output writes a `for` that returns the generator's element unchanged. It is graded violated under the table row `for path <- paths, File.read!(path) =~ ~r/Yex/, do: path` | `Enum.filter(paths, &(File.read!(&1) =~ ~r/Yex/))`, because the comprehension only keeps some elements and returns each as it is, with the test in the generator's pattern instead of a filter expression; haiku-1 (line 116) and sonnet-1 (line 172) write the same step with Enum.filter/2. If the row is meant only for a `for` with a filter expression, this verdict reverts to clean, and the `for`s that extract a field, such as for {:param, name} <- segments, do: name, are not this shape either way. Captures, haiku-1 line 141 (&{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id}) is violated by "or passes `&2` before `&1` or the same placeholder twice", the standard 2026-10-30-check-2 and 2026-10-30-check-3 applied to the identical line; grades before that text held it clean. With, sonnet-1 lines 126-127 and 141-142 nest a case on a second fallible call inside a one-step `with`, the third Instead-of of the rule, decided by "A body that calls another function that can fail and works on its result makes that call the second step, chained with a second `<-` instead of a nested `case`"; the same lines are listed under Keep functions short and at one level of detail as the 2026-10-21-check sonnet-1 grade listed them. The one-step `with`s whose body is one call (haiku-2 60-62; sonnet-1 90-92, 153-155; sonnet-2 74-76, 93-95, 109-111) are tail calls and stay clean.

Unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-31 standard. Atoms, dates, money and processes: clean in all five (every run uses Decimal, and Enum.max(DateTime) or Enum.max_by(..., DateTime)). Lists: opus-1 (line 116), haiku-1 (line 59) and sonnet-2 (line 195) prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean because grouping, counting, a max and a sort with a tie-break do not depend on the order. Inline `->`: haiku-1 lines 59-60 are the shape the 2026-10-31 grade held as a table, and its line 129 fn clause is 71 characters, held within "about 70" as that grade held the same length. Name a step: the tagged literals {:ok, / %{ ... }} (haiku-1 75-82, sonnet-1 101-108, sonnet-2 49-56) are held clean as data with no computation to name. Naming: acc (haiku-2) and group (haiku-1) are held to the earlier standard. Other rules: haiku-2's Order struct has no @type t, listed under the struct rule as 2026-10-22-check and 2026-10-30-check-3 listed it; haiku-1 and haiku-2 match the five required keys in a multi-line head with a catch-all clause below, held clean under the head rule as earlier grades held it.
